scenes.title: Explain Analyze
scenes.narration: EXPLAIN ANALYZE goes a step beyond a plain plan by actually running the query and reporting what really happened.

scenes.title: EXPLAIN vs EXPLAIN ANALYZE

right.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
points: Shows actual rows next to estimates

scenes.narration: Plain EXPLAIN only shows the estimated plan and never touches your data, drawing its numbers from statistics. EXPLAIN ANALYZE, by contrast, actually executes the query and reports the real time spent in each operator alongside the actual number of rows it produced.

scenes.title: Run it on a query
scenes.code:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT c.region, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.region;
scenes.narration: Here we ask EXPLAIN ANALYZE to profile a grouped join. The engine executes it for real and annotates every node. For each operator you will see the estimated rows, the actual rows, and the actual time in milliseconds, letting you compare prediction against reality.

scenes.title: What the actuals reveal
bullets: Cardinality misestimates where actual rows dwarf the estimate
The specific operator that consumes most of the runtime
Loops executed many times, multiplying a small per-loop cost
scenes.narration: The actual numbers expose cardinality misestimates, where the real row count dwarfs what the optimizer guessed. They pinpoint the single operator eating most of the runtime. And they reveal loops that ran thousands of times, turning a tiny per-iteration cost into a serious bottleneck.

scenes.text: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement. Running it on an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE will change your data — wrap those in a transaction and roll back.
scenes.narration: Remember that EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the statement for real, so profiling an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE will actually modify data. Wrap such statements in a transaction and roll it back when you are done.

scenes.text: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to compare estimated versus actual rows and timing, and let the biggest gap point you to the real problem.
scenes.narration: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to compare estimated and actual rows and timing, then let the biggest gap between the two guide you straight to the real problem.
